title: Y-intercept after a vertical translation of y=x squared
source: Theory P1-2.5 Quick check 1 (vector (0,4), y-intercept 4); book Key point 2.6, new numbers
stem: The graph of \(y=x^2\) is translated by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix}0\\{a|int}\end{pmatrix}\). What is the \(y\)-intercept of the resulting graph?

title: Vertical translation that maps y=2x to y=2x+k
source: Theory P1-2.5 Quick check 2 (k=5); book Key point 2.6, new numbers
stem: The graph of \(y=2x\) can be translated to the graph of \(y=2x+{k|int}\) by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix}0\\c\end{pmatrix}\). What is the value of \(c\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: A translation by \(\begin{pmatrix}0\\{k|int}\end{pmatrix}\) adds {k|int} to the output, so \(c={K|int}\).

title: Image of a point after a horizontal translation
source: Theory P1-2.5 Quick check 3 (point (1,2) translated by (3,0) has x-coordinate 4); book Key point 2.7, new numbers
stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) is translated by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix}{h|int}\\0\end{pmatrix}\). The point \(({p|int}, 2)\) lies on \(y=f(x)\). What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the image of this point?

title: Equation after translating y=x^2+2x-5 by the vector (-1, 3)

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2022), Question 4(a) only, including the official column vector. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Part 4(b) is omitted (a stretch, which belongs to 2.7).

stem:
This question is 9709/13/M/J/22 Question 4(a), taken from the official QP.

(a) The curve with equation \(y=x^2+2x-5\) is translated by \(\begin{pmatrix}-1\\3\end{pmatrix}\).
Find the equation of the translated curve, giving your answer in the form \(y=ax^2+bx+c\).  [3]

steps.name: M1
steps.text_tex: A translation by \(\begin{pmatrix}-1\\3\end{pmatrix}\) means replace \(x\) by \(x-(-1)=x+1\), and add 3. So \(y=(x+1)^2+2(x+1)-5+3\).
steps.note: MS 4(a): M1 for dealing with the -1 (the horizontal component) and M1 for dealing with the 3 (the vertical component).

steps.name: M2
steps.note: The second M1 is for correctly applying the other component of the vector.

steps.name: A
steps.note: MS 4(a): A1 for y=x^2+4x+1. Answer only is given full marks. Independent: expand (x+1)^2+2(x+1)-5+3 = x^2+4x+1.
